service.description: Planned blocks (unavailabilityKindEnumId RukPlanned, impl-maintenance P15): a block of the resource from fromDate (now when empty, a future one allowed) to thruDate (required, END_REQUIRED; at most a year, INTERVAL_INVALID), with its reason (a closure by default, Manufacturing's offline time RurOffline) and, for Maintenance, the work order it is for; Maintenance's entry is a resource administrator (RESOURCE_POLICY_EDIT) or supervisor of the resource's scope, Manufacturing's a scheduler or method engineer (PRODUCTION_SCHEDULE or METHOD_RESOURCES) of a work center of an organization they work for (PERMISSION_DENIED, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE). Bookings it covers (a facility's and those inside it) are kept, never cancelled, and answered (affectedBookingIds) for review. Otherwise: Record an actual outage of a resource, equipment (assetId: an asset that is not stock) or a facility (facilityId), exactly one (design-maintenance Downtime RecordDowntime, review Y3), or link the one that is open: with the resource locked, its open actual outage in force (no thruDate, not superseded) is answered (linked true) and nothing else is written but the work order's link, so two faults of one resource are one outage; else a new one of kind RukActual from fromDate (now when empty), open, or ended at thruDate (a past outage, a supervisor's or resource administrator's), with the reason (ResourceUnavailabilityReason, its planned or unplanned classification kept), the description, and its source: the production downtime or the maintenance work order and step. A work order named links the outage (MaintenanceWorkOrder.resourceUnavailabilityId). Bookings of the resource over it are kept and answered by id (affectedBookingIds). Nothing here ends an outage: end#ResourceUnavailability restores the resource. Two entry points, checked by data: Manufacturing's, sourceProductionDowntimeId an equipment-fault stop of the asset in an organization the user operates (PRODUCTION_OPERATE or PRODUCTION_SUPERVISE), a stop not corrected and with no outage yet, the outage from its start, open and an equipment fault (SOURCE_INVALID otherwise), as ProductionDowntime.js records it; and Maintenance's, MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE or MAINTENANCE_RESOURCE_EDIT on a resource of the user's maintenance scope, or MAINTENANCE_EXECUTE on the work order (or its step) assigned to the user (workEffortId) that targets it, with a reason (REASON_INVALID). Refuses a kind other than RukActual (KIND_INVALID), no resource or two (RESOURCE_REQUIRED), stock or a missing asset (ASSET_INVALID), a kind other than RukActual or RukPlanned (KIND_INVALID), a resource or work outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), another permission (PERMISSION_DENIED), a technician without work (WORK_REQUIRED) or on work not theirs (NOT_ASSIGNED), work that is no work order on the resource (WORK_INVALID), a step of other work (STEP_INVALID), a source that is no equipment fault of the asset (SOURCE_INVALID), and a start or end in the future or an end before the start (INTERVAL_INVALID).

parameter.name: workEffortId
parameter.description: The maintenance work order (its root) the outage is recorded from

parameter.name: linked
parameter.description: True when an open outage of the resource was answered

service.description: The actual outages of the user's maintenance scope (a work or resource read: MAINTENANCE_VIEW, _ASSIGNED_VIEW or _RESOURCE_VIEW; PERMISSION_DENIED without), newest first, in force unless includeCorrected, scoped and filtered in the query before paging: one outage, organization, equipment, facility (with those inside it and the equipment there), reason, planned or unplanned (planned Y or N), open or ended (open true or false), source (production or work), a work order (the outages it recorded or linked; it must be readable) and a period (fromDate, thruDate overlapping). Each row carries its resource, interval and elapsed time (open ones to now), reason and classification, production context (the stop's work center, reason and run, and how many stops link it), the work orders recorded with or linked, who recorded and who restored it with the disposition, its corrections, the bookings it affects (a count), the open work orders a restoration leaves open (openWorkList), and canRestore and canCorrect for the user. With resourceUnavailabilityId, history is its correction chain. A holder of every organization with an active one lists that organization's. With unavailabilityKindEnumId RukPlanned (Blackouts, P15) the planned blocks, each with its state (planned, in effect, ended, withdrawn, corrected), its source (a blackout, a work order, production offline), the bookings it covers until it ends (affectedBookingCount, flagged for review) and canCorrect and canEnd for a resource administrator or supervisor.

A correction of an outage in force, a maintenance supervisor's or resource administrator's (MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE or MAINTENANCE_RESOURCE_EDIT, PERMISSION_DENIED) in the user's scope, with its reason (REASON_REQUIRED): a new row with the corrected start, the end of an ended outage, the reason and the description, which keeps who recorded and who restored it, and the corrected row kept with its values, superseded by the new one (supersession, design §6); the work orders linked to it are linked to the new row. Refuses an outage outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one already corrected (OUTAGE_CORRECTED), a changed revision (REVISION_CHANGED), an end on an open outage, which restoration gives (OUTAGE_OPEN), a reason that is no downtime reason (REASON_INVALID) and an interval in the future or ending before it starts (INTERVAL_INVALID). A planned block (P15, replacing the P5 review's KIND_INVALID) is corrected the same way, as a new row in force over the one kept, by either of record#'s entry points for blocks, its end required and a future interval allowed; Manufacturing's withdraw ends the row in force of the block it names.

parameter.name: affectedBookingCount
parameter.description: A planned block's: the bookings it covers

service.description: The restoration of a resource, the only end of an actual outage (design §6 RestoreResource, §7.1): a maintenance supervisor's or resource administrator's (MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE or MAINTENANCE_RESOURCE_EDIT, PERMISSION_DENIED) in the user's scope, at thruDate (now when empty, not before the start nor in the future), with the disposition, available for use (MdispAvailable) or usable with restrictions (MdispRestricted), and the readiness evidence (endComments). Maintenance work orders linked to the outage that are still open stay open: the answer lists them (openWorkList, as find# does for the dialog), and restoring while any is open needs the reason (openWorkReason, kept on the row; OPEN_WORK names them without one; the user's call of Nov 12). No work order ends an outage: closing the production downtime that recorded it, completing a work order or cancelling one ends nothing, so two work orders on one resource cannot each end the other's. Refuses an outage outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one corrected (OUTAGE_CORRECTED), one ended (OUTAGE_ENDED), a changed revision (REVISION_CHANGED), no disposition (DISPOSITION_REQUIRED) or another one (DISPOSITION_INVALID) and an end out of its interval (INTERVAL_INVALID). A planned block (P15) is ended now by either of record#'s entry points for blocks (resultCode ENDED), or withdrawn when it has not begun (WITHDRAWN, its end set to its start), with no disposition; the row is kept.

parameter.name: openWorkReason
parameter.description: Required while a linked work order is open

parameter.name: openWorkList
parameter.description: The linked work orders still open (workEffortId, workEffortName, statusText, text), which stay open

service.description: The one availability read of a resource, equipment (assetId) or a facility (facilityId), from fromDate (now) to thruDate (two weeks later; at most 92 days, INTERVAL_INVALID): its requested and assigned bookings, its planned blocks and actual outages in force (a facility's own and those of the facilities above it), kept apart (kind assigned, requested, planned or actual) with a safe label: Busy for an event the user may not see (no id, no title), a block's reason, "Out of service". excludeWorkEffortId leaves out an event and its series. Any signed-in user; no description, organizer or attendee of a block or a hidden event.

parameter.name: intervalList
parameter.description: fromDate, thruDate, fromText, thruText, kind, kindText, label, workEffortId, resourceUnavailabilityId, hard

service.description: The bookable equipment and facilities (bookable Y; no stock, no closed facility) of the user's maintenance scope (design Resources ResourceRows): RESOURCE_POLICY_VIEW or _EDIT or a resource read lists the scope's, a booking approver (RESOURCE_BOOKING_VIEW_ASSIGNED) only the resources they approve now (PERMISSION_DENIED without). Filters: resourceType (asset or facility), text (the name), facilityId (that facility, those inside it and the equipment there) and managed (Y: with a policy in force, N: without). Each row: the resource, its type and location, capacity and features, managed and the policy in words, the longest booking, the approvers, the block in force now or the next within two weeks (blockText), the requests waiting (pendingCount) and canEdit.

A resource's booking policy (design ResourcePolicyDetail BookingPolicy): the policy in force (none: the resource is not managed and keeps the approver fallback), its words, the history of policies, the approvers (current and later, with their dates), the setup findings (approval required and no approver; not bookable) and canEdit. Read by a RESOURCE_POLICY_VIEW or _EDIT holder or resource reader of its organization, or one of its booking approvers (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE otherwise).

A resource's booking policy from fromDate (now when empty, never in the past, DATE_PAST), a RESOURCE_POLICY_EDIT holder's of its organization (PERMISSION_DENIED, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE): bookable, the approval mode (RbamAutomatic or RbamApprovers), the horizon in days, the longest booking in minutes (whole numbers of at least 1, VALUE_INVALID), the time zone and whether a soft conflict may be overridden; or endPolicy, the resource unmanaged from then (POLICY_NONE when it has none). The policy in force and any later one end then (one beginning later is withdrawn); a change names the policy in force's revision (REVISION_CHANGED) and its reason (REASON_REQUIRED). A change applies to new and changed bookings: the ones already made are kept, and impactList names those it no longer allows, for review (as preview#). Approval required with no approver is accepted and refuses every booking until one is named (a setup finding).

What store#ResourceBookingPolicy with the same values would mean (design PolicyImpact), a RESOURCE_POLICY_EDIT holder's: each requested or assigned booking of the next 180 days from its date that the new rules no longer allow (not bookable, longer than the maximum, past the horizon, approval required with no approver), with a safe label, its interval, state, finding and consequence (kept, for review), and the setup findings. Nothing is written.

A booking approver of a resource (design ResourcePolicyDetail BookingApprovers), a RESOURCE_POLICY_EDIT holder's of its organization: the person (PARTY_INVALID otherwise) added as a dated BookingApprover row (FacilityParty, or AssetPartyAssignment for equipment) from fromDate (now), or, with end or thruDate, ended then (APPROVER_NONE when they approve none of it). Ending the last current approver while requests wait needs another (replacementPartyId, added from the end) or the reason they are left unresolved (unresolvedReason; APPROVER_PENDING without). Maintenance's lifecycle participant hands a leaver's approvals over through it.

The bookings waiting for a decision (design BookingRequests BookingRows): of the resources the user approves now (a current BookingApprover, RESOURCE_BOOKING_VIEW_ASSIGNED or _APPROVE), or of the resources of the user's maintenance scope for a policy reader or supervisor (RESOURCE_POLICY_VIEW, _EDIT, MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE), read only (PERMISSION_DENIED for anyone else). status requested (the default), assigned or denied; not over yet; filters: one resource (facilityId or assetId), the organizer (requesterPartyId), a period (fromDate, thruDate overlapping) and the resource's name (text). Soonest first. Each row: the resource, the event's span now (whenText, recurring), the organizer, its purpose when the user may open the event (else "Not shared with you"), the requester's notes, the policy in words, the bookings it clashes with (an event the user may not see is Busy), how long it waited, canDecide (an approver of it holding RESOURCE_BOOKING_APPROVE) and what a decision names: expectedStatusId, expectedFromDate and expectedThruDate.

A requested booking approved or denied (design BookingDecision, §7.1 approval; the first path that decides one, F15): by a current BookingApprover of the resource (NOT_APPROVER) holding RESOURCE_BOOKING_APPROVE (PERMISSION_DENIED), with the resource locked (the work centers above a facility first). Refuses a booking no longer requested or a cancelled event (STATE_CHANGED, also when expectedStatusId differs) and a meeting that moved from the span decided on (expectedFromDate, expectedThruDate; SPAN_CHANGED). An approval rechecks the availability through the booking guard: an outage or block (RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), the managed resource's rules, and the assigned bookings over the span (CONFLICT; a request waiting holds nothing against this one, so two approvers of overlapping requests cannot both assign: the second is refused); an override with allowConflicts and overrideReason where the policy allows it and the user holds RESOURCE_BOOKING_OVERRIDE. A denial needs its reason (REASON_REQUIRED), kept in the booking's comments ("Denied: ..."). The booking's approval notices leave every inbox, and the organizer is told on ResourceBookingNotice.

parameter.name: expectedFromDate
parameter.description: The span decided on (a time stamp or milliseconds)

service.description: Several requested bookings decided alike (design BulkBookingDecision): bookingList, each {workEffortId, facilityId or assetId, expectedStatusId, expectedFromDate, expectedThruDate} or its key text "facility|id|workEffortId|fromMs|thruMs" (comma separated; at most 100; SELECTION_REQUIRED for none), each through decide#ResourceBooking in its own transaction; a failure is named in resultList (reasonCode, message), logged, and the rest go on.

The ResourceBooking topic's approve service (Commons' approvals inbox; approve#NotificationMessage calls it as the user deciding): the notice's booking (recordId the event; message facilityId or assetId, the span and state it was sent with) approved through decide#ResourceBooking, which checks the user again; a meeting moved since is refused SPAN_CHANGED.
The ResourceBooking topic's refuse service: the notice's booking denied with the reason (REASON_REQUIRED), through decide#ResourceBooking.
